ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; E is located on side AB, D is located on side AC; segment EC and BD intersect at O inside the triangle; segment DE has been connected. Because E, O, C are collinear, and B, O, D are collinear, ∠DEO can be written as ∠DEC, and ∠CBO can be written as ∠DBC, namely ∠DEC = ∠DBC. Also because A, D, C are collinear, ∠ADE is the exterior angle at D of triangle CDE, therefore ∠ADE = ∠DCE + ∠DEC. Since CD and CA are on the same line, ∠DCE = ∠ACE; then from the given condition ∠ABD = ∠ACE, obtain ∠ADE = ∠ACE + ∠DBC = ∠ABD + ∠DBC = ∠ABC. At the same time, AD is on AC, and AE is on AB, so ∠DAE = ∠CAB. Therefore triangle ADE and triangle ABC are similar, with the correspondence A↔A, D↔B, E↔C. Thus the corresponding sides are proportional: AE/AC = DE/BC. It is known that DE/BC = 2/3, so AE/AC = 2/3.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A is the top vertex of triangle ABC, B and C are the base vertices, E lies on AB, D lies on AC, the cevians EC and BD meet at O, and segment DE is drawn. Because E,O,C are collinear and B,O,D are collinear, rewrite this as ∠DEC = ∠DBC. Since A,D,C are collinear, ∠ADE is the exterior angle of triangle CDE, so ∠ADE = ∠DCE + ∠DEC = ∠ACE + ∠DBC. Substitute ∠ACE = ∠ABD to get ∠ADE = ∠ABD + ∠DBC = ∠ABC. Also ∠DAE = ∠CAB because AD lies on AC and AE lies on AB. Therefore triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC in the order A↔A, D↔B, E↔C. Hence corresponding sides give AE/AC = DE/BC = 2/3.
